message.content:
Roger presented for his initial intake session reporting that he is not feeling the greatest and is currently navigating a tough time. He stated that focusing has been particularly difficult lately, which causes him to feel distressed because when his focus feels off, many other aspects of his life feel off as well.

We discussed his current living situation, noting that he is staying at the Turning Point shelter while collecting disability benefits for a traumatic brain injury. Roger shared a history of substance use but expressed no current desire to use substances because they cause too many problems for him. His anxiety and depression scores were recorded at 2 and 3 respectively, indicating these levels are not too bad relative to his overall distress. The primary source of his current discomfort appears to be the lack of focus rather than severe mood symptoms.

The intervention utilized was active listening and psychoeducation regarding the cognitive impacts of traumatic brain injury on concentration. We validated his frustration with his attentional difficulties and normalized the connection between focus and general emotional stability. Roger responded well to this validation, appearing more relaxed after acknowledging that his struggles with focus are linked to his TBI history. He engaged openly in the discussion about his substance use history without defensiveness. We agreed to monitor his focus levels closely in future sessions to determine if additional cognitive strategies are needed.
